searchText: ### **EIP-7928 Breakout #7** call — [Nov 19, 2025, 14:00 UTC](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1810) Countdown: <t:1763560800:R> Location: Zoom (livestreamed on YouTube) Agenda: * Update on gas used values in BALs (rejected) * Syncing and BALs (pruning?) * Client and devnet updates Another topic that I would like to talk about is bal over p2p aka persisting of BALs. Not sure if this was discussed previously. Have talked with the team and most logical things for us is to not serve it over eth p2p, to not store it at all. if it's not served over devp2p, then BALs cannot be used for the removal of snap sync healing phase. IMO it makes sense to keep and serve them for recent N blocks, so that we can greatly simplify snap sync Should they be part of snap sync? This is hard to enforce last N blocks, maybe having it optional could work? The BAL is part of the block right? So wouldn’t it be persisted and propagated the same way a block is? I think just having a message to query them by block hash from a node would be nice You want just the BAL without the block? Adding it to db will increase db footprint so we need to treat it differently, to drop it You want to compute them on demand? Look at them like a blobs, they are used to sync then dropped. What is the storage impact we are talking about here? Will a super node or archive node treat this differently? roughly 2x the current block size it's significant Even with compression? I'm not factoring compression here Seems a bit early to be optimizing for this imo lets first get some numbers on just storing the block with BALs? Maybe worth adding to the call agenda > Seems a bit early to be optimizing for this imo lets first get some numbers on just storing the block with BALs? We talked about this in Berlin, consensus was to drop them from db, so this is nothing new and it looks logical. Discussion that i wanted to have is about p2p Will put that on the agenda! Have we looked into the compression ratio? Just curious now The reason I said early is because imo we should focus on getting a stable devnet release from all clients where they can generate valid BALs and this seems like something we can focus on for a later devnet I will need to ask, for us it could be a more effort to save it to db than to just drop it. I see, interesting It sounds strange, how can reth drop the BAL? It is part of the block body and we don't have optional fields, so when dropping the bal at some time you'd need to recalculate it on the fly to serve api or p2p block requests? Recalculating it seems also really expensive, as you need the prestate to distinguish between storage reads & updates? [bal v1.6.0](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/releases/tag/bal%40v1.6.0) was just released with many updates and reenforcing tests for the specs. As always please flag anything that may come up. I am going to focus on making sure hive can run these now as it seems to be having some issues. It will be good to get this working so we can see some real numbers in the dashboard. Hive changes are looking good 👌🏽

### **EIP-7928 Breakout #7** call — [Nov 19, 2025, 14:00 UTC](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1810)
Countdown: <t:1763560800:R>
Location: Zoom (livestreamed on YouTube)

Agenda:
* Update on gas used values in BALs (rejected)
* Syncing and BALs (pruning?)
* Client and devnet updates

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content: Another topic that I would like to talk about is bal over p2p aka persisting of BALs. Not sure if this was discussed previously. Have talked with the team and most logical things for us is to not serve it over eth p2p, to not store it at all.

excerpts.author: jwasinger
excerpts.content: if it's not served over devp2p, then BALs cannot be used for the removal of snap sync healing phase.

excerpts.author: jwasinger
excerpts.content: IMO it makes sense to keep and serve them for recent N blocks, so that we can greatly simplify snap sync

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content: Should they be part of snap sync?

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content: This is hard to enforce last N blocks, maybe having it optional could work?

excerpts.author: qu0b
excerpts.content: The BAL is part of the block right? So wouldn’t it be persisted and propagated the same way a block is?

excerpts.author: jwasinger
excerpts.content: I think just having a message to query them by block hash from a node would be nice

excerpts.author: qu0b
excerpts.content: You want just the BAL without the block?

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content: Adding it to db will increase db footprint so we need to treat it differently, to drop it

excerpts.author: qu0b
excerpts.content: You want to compute them on demand?

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content: Look at them like a blobs, they are used to sync then dropped.

excerpts.author: qu0b
excerpts.content: What is the storage impact we are talking about here?

excerpts.author: qu0b
excerpts.content: Will a super node or archive node treat this differently?

excerpts.author: jwasinger
excerpts.content: roughly 2x the current block size

excerpts.author: jwasinger
excerpts.content: it's significant

excerpts.author: qu0b
excerpts.content: Even with compression?

excerpts.author: jwasinger
excerpts.content: I'm not factoring compression here

excerpts.author: qu0b
excerpts.content: Seems a bit early to be optimizing for this imo lets first get some numbers on just storing the block with BALs?

excerpts.author: qu0b
excerpts.content: Maybe worth adding to the call agenda

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content:
> Seems a bit early to be optimizing for this imo lets first get some numbers on just storing the block with BALs?
We talked about this in Berlin, consensus was to drop them from db, so this is nothing new and it looks logical. Discussion that i wanted to have is about p2p

excerpts.author: nero_eth
excerpts.content: Will put that on the agenda!

excerpts.author: qu0b
excerpts.content: Have we looked into the compression ratio?

excerpts.author: qu0b
excerpts.content: Just curious now

excerpts.author: qu0b
excerpts.content: The reason I said early is because imo we should focus on getting a stable devnet release from all clients where they can generate valid BALs and this seems like something we can focus on for a later devnet

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content: I will need to ask, for us it could be a more effort to save it to db than to just drop it.

excerpts.author: qu0b
excerpts.content: I see, interesting

excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content:
It sounds strange, how can reth drop the BAL?
It is part of the block body and we don't have optional fields, so when dropping the bal at some time you'd need to recalculate it on the fly to serve api or p2p block requests?
Recalculating it seems also really expensive, as you need the prestate to distinguish between storage reads & updates?
